nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition of Ni(OH)2 nanosheets on carbon cloth from Ni(NO3)2·6H2O or NiSO4·6H2O aqueous solution at optimal deposition time of 420 s (300 s and 540 s show inferior performance).

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: electrodeposition time of 420 s is the optimal

nodes.source_text: The effect of electrodeposition time on the electrochemical performance of the Ni(OH)2/CC electrode was firstly investigated; other deposition times of 300 and 540 s show inferior catalytic activities (Fig. S5†), suggesting that 420 s is the optimal electrodeposition time in our study.

nodes.name: Ni electrodeposition on Ni(OH)2

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows diffraction peaks at 26.0° from graphitic carbon (002), 34.3° and 60.1° from nickel hydroxide hydrate (012) and (110) planes (JCPDS No. 38-0715), and 44.5° and 51.8° from metallic Ni (111) and (200) planes (JCPDS No. 65-2865).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the final product. The diffraction peak at 26.0° is attributed to the (002) reflection of graphitic carbon from CC. Two diffraction peaks at around 34.3 and 60.1° correspond to the (012) and (110) planes of nickel hydroxide hydrate (JCPDS No. 38-0715), respectively. The additional diffraction peaks at about 44.5 and 51.8° are indexed to the (111) and (200) planes of metallic Ni (JCPDS No. 65-2865).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p spectrum shows metallic Ni peak at 852.5 eV (Ni 2p3/2), Ni²⁺ peaks at 875.3 eV (Ni 2p1/2) and 857.4 eV (Ni 2p3/2), O 1s peak at 531.7 eV from OH⁻ in Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S1†, the Ni 2p3/2 peak at 852.5 eV is assigned to the characteristic feature of metallic Ni. The strong peaks of Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 at 875.3 and 857.4 eV with two shakeup satellites indicate that Ni is mainly in the Ni²⁺ oxidation state. The major O 1s peak at 531.7 eV is assigned to OH⁻ presumably derived from Ni(OH)₂ (Fig. S1b†).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows full coverage of CC with Ni(OH)₂@Ni nanosheets, with Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet films thickness of 137-155 nm after Ni deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of Ni(OH)₂@Ni/CC (Fig. 1b and c) indicate the full coverage of CC with Ni(OH)₂@Ni nanosheets and the thickness of Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet films slightly increases to about 137-155 nm after Ni deposition (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni nanoparticles covering Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet surface; HRTEM reveals lattice fringe of 0.232 nm for (015) plane of Ni(OH)₂ and 0.203 nm for (111) plane of Ni phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM image of a Ni(OH)₂@Ni nanosheet (Fig. 1e) shows that the surface of Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets is covered with Ni nanoparticles. Fig. 1f reveals a lattice fringe with an interplanar distance of 0.232 nm corresponding to the (015) plane of Ni(OH)₂. The typical interfringe distance of 0.203 nm corresponds to the lattice spacing of the (111) plane of the Ni phase (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Ni(OH)₂@Ni/CC is 86.1 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm plot shows that the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area of Ni(OH)₂@Ni/CC is 86.1 m² g⁻¹ (Fig. S3a†).

nodes.characterization_summary: BJH average pore size of Ni(OH)₂@Ni/CC film is 5.7 nm and pore volume is 0.12 cm³ g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Barrett–Joyner–Halenda (BJH) average pore size and pore volume of Ni(OH)₂@Ni/CC film are 5.7 nm and 0.12 cm³ g⁻¹, respectively.
